Marisol asked one question and the draft answers it plainly and honestly: there isn't time for a 22. The reason it gives is sound. A long run takes 2–3 weeks to pay off, and she already has a 20 behind her. That should also ease some of her worry about the new date.

The plan works as a first taper week. It adds up to 36 mi against her 42 this week, and the long run drops to 13. The paces fit her 3:45 goal: 8:35/mi is goal marathon pace, and easy runs sit around 9:55 or under 145 bpm. Nothing breaks a must-never check, and her rest days stay on Monday and Friday. Every day is clear enough to run as written.

Why it's a 4 and not a 5:
- The opening contradicts itself. It says the taper starts now, then calls this "the last meaningful week before race prep."
- It speaks to her anxiety only through the reasoning, never directly.
- It names a 17 on Sep 27 and gives dates for both long runs. None of that is on the card, so I can't check it.

shown:
── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Race moved up means the taper starts now, so skip the 22 and treat this as the last meaningful week before race prep. …
Answers: No, there is not time for a 22-miler, and you do not need one. You already have a 20 (Sep 13) and a solid 17 (Sep 27) in the legs, and the aerobic gains from a long run take 2 – 3 weeks to show up.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to open the taper and recover from Sunday's 17.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Loosens the legs after the long run.
Wed: quality, 8 mi with 5 mi at 8:35/mi in the middle, 1 mi easy warm-up and 2 mi easy…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, conversational. Flush out Wednesday without…
Fri: rest. Keep it a true rest day to set up the weekend.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, then 4 x 20 sec strides on flat ground with full walk recovery. Keeps…
Sun: long, 13 mi, first 10 mi easy around 9:55/mi, last 3 mi at 8:35/mi. Final…
